name: find-text
description: A `find` by `text` searches the requirements alone: those whose `id`, `title` and `description` hold every word of the phrase — each query word equal to or a prefix of a distinct word of that text, never a substring — answered in `id` order, at most sixteen, each with its address, a one-line identity (the id and the title, at most 72 characters) and the words it matched; `more` counts the rest, and the baseline token rides along. The requirement's `document` field is never answered.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model with two requirements added: `REQ_EXAMPLE_002`, whose text holds `example` and `functionality` and which names its source document, and `REQ_EXAMPLE_003`, whose text holds `example` and not `function`. `REQ_EXAMPLE_001`'s description holds both.
context.notes: A `find` reads the model and writes nothing: no scope, no baseline in the request, no audit record. `function` is a prefix of `functionality`, so it matches; `REQ_EXAMPLE_003` holds one of the two words and is not answered.
